web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Four Engines Under One Digital Roof
question: How does Protean actually make money across Tax, Pension, Identity, and New DPI segments, and how does each workflow operate for a real customer?

epigraph.quote: We are moving from being priced per API call to being priced per journey, per outcome.
epigraph.author: Ajay Rajan, MD & CEO, Q1 FY27 Earnings Call

web_blocks.title: Revenue Mix Evolution: From Tax Concentration to Four Pillars

web_blocks.html: Protean reports sales across four operating pillars: Tax Services, CRA Pension Services, Identity Services, and New Businesses [10, 11]. New Businesses covers Open Digital Ecosystems and turnkey DPI deals [10, 11]. In FY26, total revenue reached a record ₹998 crore, up 18.7% YoY from ₹841 crore in FY25 [10, 15]. However, ₹44 crore came from one-time storage fee recoveries booked in Q4 FY26 [10, 15]. Excluding that one-off item, core revenue grew roughly 13.4% YoY. By Q2 FY27, New Businesses reached 16% of sales (₹42 crore), while Tax Services stayed near 45–50% [10, 17].

web_blocks.caption: Protean eGov Segmental Revenue & Growth Profile (FY25–H1 FY27)
rows: ₹42 Cr (~16% mix); driven by ASK & RFP rollouts [10, 17]
web_blocks.takeaway: Tax and Pension still supply ~80% of revenue, while New Businesses tripled in FY26 and reached 16% of quarterly sales by Q2 FY27—requiring careful margin tracking as legacy tax faces PAN 2.0.

web_blocks.title: 1. Tax Services (PAN, TIN & TAN): End-to-End Citizen Workflow

web_blocks.html: Tax Services brought in ₹498 crore in FY26 (+17.5% YoY) [1, 11]. The unit handled over 4.7 crore PAN cards at a 59% market share against rival UTIITSL [1, 11]. That share rose to 65.8% in Q2 FY27 [1, 11]. Take a real-world example: a first-time salaried worker in Pune applies for a PAN card. She uses a local center or Protean's web portal and pays a set fee upfront via UPI. The fee is ₹107 for a physical card or ₹72 for an e-PAN. Protean checks her Aadhaar data, runs duplicate checks with the tax office, and creates the 10-digit PAN. It then mails the card via India Post and pays print, post, and agent fees from that fee [10]. Since users pay first and agents are paid later, this unit ran on negative working capital. Tax Services also handles TAN applications and e-TDS returns for corporate employers.

web_blocks.title: 2. CRA Pension Services (NPS, APY, UPS): The 97% Annuity Moat

web_blocks.html: CRA Services earned ₹304 crore in FY26 (+7.5% YoY) and ₹80 crore in Q2 FY27 [11, 12, 17]. It serves 9.39 crore total members, up from 5.13 crore in FY22 [11, 12, 17]. Protean holds a 97% share across NPS, Atal Pension Yojana (APY), and the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) [11, 12, 17]. When an engineer in Bengaluru joins a firm, or a rural worker joins APY, Protean issues a PRAN. It keeps the master ledger of monthly inflows, settles funds with Axis Bank, and guides fund managers on NAV units [12]. Protean earns a PFRDA-set opening fee, an annual account fee, and ₹3.75 per transaction [22]. That compares with ₹3.50 at CAMS and ₹3.36 at KFintech [22]. New schemes like NPS Vatsalya and UPS grow the user base, though PFRDA fee resets cap pricing power [21].

web_blocks.title: 3. Identity Services & 4. New DPI Ecosystems: From APIs to Bundled Journeys

web_blocks.html: Identity Services earned ₹92 crore in FY26 and ₹27 crore in Q2 FY27 (+24% YoY) [11, 17]. It powers real-time checks for banks, brokers, and fintech apps [11, 17]. When an investor opens a demat account on a phone app, Protean APIs run an Online PAN Check. They pull Aadhaar e-KYC XML data and trigger Aadhaar e-Sign on the PDF within seconds. Basic API pricing faced stiff price cuts between FY24 (₹111 crore) and FY26 (₹92 crore) [13, 19]. So Protean now bundles eSignPro, fraud checks, bank-statement tools, and CKYC into Rise with Protean. It charges per full onboarding flow instead of per raw API call [13, 19].

New Businesses earned ₹103 crore in FY26 and ₹42 crore in Q2 FY27 [10, 17]. It houses Protean's newer bets [10, 17]. Under a ₹1,160 crore UIDAI contract, Protean runs 190 district Aadhaar Seva Kendras [16]. Citizens walk in for biometric updates and new enrolments on a fee-per-task basis [16]. Protean is also building CERSAI's CKYCRR 2.0 registry across RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, and PFRDA [13, 18]. It is building the ₹100 crore Bima Sugam insurance hub and running ONDC and Kochi Metro gateways [13, 18]. It also runs an RBI-licensed Account Aggregator and sells DPI in a Box abroad in Ethiopia (₹25 crore) and Morocco [13, 18].

Profitability differs sharply across these four engines. Legacy Tax Services and CRA Pensions earn healthy cash margins on mature software rails. By contrast, Identity APIs face stiff price pressure from fintech rivals and state tools. Meanwhile, New Businesses absorb upfront hardware, lease, and staff costs ahead of full billing [13, 17]. Until those 190 Aadhaar Seva Kendras hit steady citizen traffic, new sales will dilute group margins.

book_paragraphs: To understand Protean without getting lost in government acronyms, follow the money across four distinct engines. Together, they generated ₹998 crore in revenue in FY26, though ₹44 crore of that figure came from a one-time storage charge recovery in the fourth quarter. Strip out that windfall and the underlying business sits near ₹954 crore—still heavily anchored in two mature franchises while two newer ones fight to scale.

The first and largest engine is Tax Services, which brought in ₹498 crore in FY26, or half of total sales. Picture a college graduate in Indore applying for her first PAN card at a neighborhood facilitation center. She pays roughly ₹107 upfront. Protean's rails verify her Aadhaar details, route the application to the Income Tax Department, print the card, and mail it. Protean collects cash on day one and pays its printing vendors and local agents later, giving the segment negative working capital. It commands nearly 60 to 66 percent of this duopoly against state-run UTIITSL. Yet this crown jewel carries an expiration date on its current architecture: after losing the PAN 2.0 backend tender to LTIMindtree in August 2025, Protean must prove its front-end facilitation network remains indispensable once the new system goes live.

The second engine is Pension Services—the Central Recordkeeping Agency for NPS, Atal Pension Yojana, and the Unified Pension Scheme—which generated ₹304 crore in FY26. Here, Protean is the undisputed ledger-keeper for 9.39 crore Indian savers, holding a 97 percent market share and capturing 95 to 96 percent of all new additions. Every time a central government clerk or corporate engineer contributes to NPS, Protean reconciles the rupee flow, tracks the NAV units, and earns a small regulated fee—₹3.75 per transaction plus annual maintenance. It is a textbook annuity, though PFRDA's periodic fee revisions keep margins tethered to regulatory goodwill.

The third engine, Identity Services, generated ₹92 crore in FY26 and rebounded 24 percent year-on-year to ₹27 crore in Q2 FY27. Every time you open a brokerage account or apply for an instant loan, Protean's APIs run an Online PAN Verification, fetch Aadhaar e-KYC records, and execute an e-Sign on your contract. Raw API pricing got squeezed by competition over the past three years, forcing management to bundle fraud checks, bank-statement analysis, and e-signing into higher-margin enterprise journeys under Rise with Protean and eSignPro.

Finally, New Businesses tripled to ₹103 crore in FY26 and hit 16 percent of quarterly revenue in Q2 FY27. When a citizen visits a district Aadhaar Seva Kendra to update biometrics, when an insurer integrates with Bima Sugam, or when a commuter books a Kochi metro ride on an open BECKN network, Protean's new rails sit underneath. Supported by a ₹1,500-plus crore order book—anchored by the ₹1,160 crore UIDAI mandate—this fourth engine is growing fastest, even as it tests Protean's ability to execute physical and milestone-based contracts.

When you step back and look at all four verticals together—Tax Services, Pension Services, Identity & Authentication, and New DPI—you notice a sharp divergence in economics. Pension Services (CRA) is a recurring, high-retention annuity tied to formal employment and financialization: every month, millions of salaried workers and Atal Pension Yojana subscribers generate tiny, predictable recordkeeping fees. Tax Services (PAN), by contrast, is event-driven and now faces architectural transition after FY27.

Meanwhile, the newer open-network bets like ONDC and Account Aggregator are strategically vital for India's digital economy, yet they remain small revenue contributors compared to legacy PAN and NPS. That is why the ₹1,160 Cr UIDAI Aadhaar Seva Kendra contract matters so much: it bridges the revenue gap in size, but it changes the operational DNA of the business from software-heavy processing to physical-center management.

Looking closely at customer stickiness across these four verticals reveals why investors must never lump all government-linked revenues into one bucket. Pension recordkeeping under PFRDA oversight has high switching costs because migrating tens of millions of subscriber ledgers carries regulatory and operational risk, whereas competitive technology-build tenders like PAN 2.0 are reset at the end of a contract cycle whenever a rival submits a sharper technical and commercial bid.
Keeping the revenue mix and real-world customer workflows of all four segments clear in your mind will make the financial forensics in Chapter 6 much easier to interpret.

book_callouts.title: Revenue Quality Is Not Uniform Across Segments
book_callouts.text: A rupee of CRA pension revenue is recurring and sticky; a rupee of turnkey RFP revenue from Bima Sugam or CKYCRR 2.0 is lumpy, milestone-billed, and capital-intensive. When evaluating Protean's headline growth, always separate annuity transaction fees from project-build billings.

book_subsections.title: Why Bundling Matters More Than Raw Volume
paragraphs: In Identity Services, Protean processes billions of verifications, yet revenue fell from ₹111 crore in FY24 to ₹92 crore in FY26. Volume without pricing power is a treadmill. By shifting enterprise clients from single ₹1 or ₹2 API calls toward end-to-end onboarding suites like Rise with Protean and eSignPro, the company is trying to capture a larger slice of each bank's customer-acquisition workflow.
Whether that commercial pivot succeeds will determine if Protean can earn software-like margins on its non-government business, or remain a low-margin utility.

book_subsections.title: The Access-Layer Thesis on Sovereign Registries
paragraphs: On CKYCRR 2.0, management has articulated a clear commercial logic: building the sovereign registry itself is only the foundation. The real recurring prize lies in monetizing the access layer—the APIs and compliance workflows that thousands of banks, insurers, and asset managers must use to search, download, and update KYC records. That access-layer model mirrors how Protean monetized Online PAN Verification on top of its PAN database, and it is the cleanest path to high-margin annuity growth if regulators permit commercial fee structures.
